::: {#exr-ar1-stationary}
#### Stationary distribution of the autoregressive chain

For the chain of @exm-ar1-chain with $\abs{\arcoef} < 1$,
find the variance $v > 0$ for which $\ndist{0, v}$
is a [stationary distribution](#def-stationary-distribution).
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#sol-ar1-stationary}

Suppose $\param^{(t)} \sim \ndist{0, v}$.
By @exm-ar1-chain, $\eps^{(t+1)}$ is independent of $\param^{(t)}$,
so $\param^{(t+1)} = \arcoef\, \param^{(t)} + \eps^{(t+1)}$,
a linear combination of independent Gaussian random variables,
is Gaussian [@CaseBerg01, Corollary 4.6.10].
By [linearity of expectation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#thm-linearity-expectation),
its mean is

$$
\ba
\E{\param^{(t+1)}}
&= \E{\arcoef\, \param^{(t)} + \eps^{(t+1)}}
&& \text{(definition of the chain)}\\
&= \arcoef\, \E{\param^{(t)}} + \E{\eps^{(t+1)}}
&& \text{(linearity of expectation)}\\
&= \arcoef \cdot 0 + 0
&& \text{(substituting the two means)}\\
&= 0
&& \text{(arithmetic)}.
\ea
$$

Independent random variables are
[uncorrelated](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#thm-indpt-uncorrelated),
so $\Cov{\param^{(t)}, \eps^{(t+1)}} = 0$,
and by the [variance of a sum of two random variables](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#cor-var-lincom2),
the variance is

$$
\ba
\Var{\param^{(t+1)}}
&= \Var{\arcoef\, \param^{(t)} + 1 \cdot \eps^{(t+1)}}
&& \text{(definition of the chain)}\\
&= \arcoef^2 \Var{\param^{(t)}} + 1^2 \Var{\eps^{(t+1)}}
  + 2 (\arcoef \cdot 1) \Cov{\param^{(t)}, \eps^{(t+1)}}
&& \text{(variance of a sum of two random variables)}\\
&= \arcoef^2 \Var{\param^{(t)}} + 1^2 \Var{\eps^{(t+1)}} + 2 (\arcoef \cdot 1) \cdot 0
&& \text{(the covariance is 0)}\\
&= \arcoef^2 \Var{\param^{(t)}} + 1^2 \Var{\eps^{(t+1)}} + 0
&& \text{($a \cdot 0 = 0$)}\\
&= \arcoef^2 \Var{\param^{(t)}} + 1^2 \Var{\eps^{(t+1)}}
&& \text{($a + 0 = a$)}\\
&= \arcoef^2 \Var{\param^{(t)}} + \Var{\eps^{(t+1)}}
&& \text{($1^2 = 1$)}\\
&= \arcoef^2 v + \Var{\eps^{(t+1)}}
&& \text{(substituting $\Var{\param^{(t)}} = v$)}\\
&= \arcoef^2 v + \sigma^2
&& \text{(substituting $\Var{\eps^{(t+1)}} = \sigma^2$)}.
\ea
$$

So $\param^{(t+1)} \sim \ndist{0, \arcoef^2 v + \sigma^2}$,
and $\ndist{0, v}$ is stationary exactly when $\arcoef^2 v + \sigma^2 = v$.
Solving for $v$:

$$
\ba
v &= \arcoef^2 v + \sigma^2
&& \text{(stationarity condition)}\\
v - \arcoef^2 v &= \sigma^2
&& \text{(subtracting $\arcoef^2 v$ from both sides)}\\
(1 - \arcoef^2)\, v &= \sigma^2
&& \text{(factoring out $v$)}\\
v &= \frac{\sigma^2}{1 - \arcoef^2}
&& \text{(dividing both sides by $1 - \arcoef^2$, which is positive because $\abs{\arcoef} < 1$)}.
\ea
$$

The stationary distribution is $\ndist{0, \sigma^2 / (1 - \arcoef^2)}$.
If instead $\abs{\arcoef} \ge 1$,
then $(1 - \arcoef^2)\, v \le 0 < \sigma^2$ for every $v > 0$,
so no $\ndist{0, v}$ distribution is stationary.

With $\arcoef = 0.9$ and $\sigma = 1$,
the stationary variance is $1 / (1 - 0.9^2) = 1 / (1 - 0.81) = 1 / 0.19 \approx `r round(1 / (1 - 0.9^2), 2)`$.
A simulated chain started far from $0$, at $\param^{(1)} = 10$,
has mean near 0 and variance near that value once its first 1,000 values are discarded:

```{r}
#| label: ar1-chain
#| code-fold: false
set.seed(11)
n_iter <- 100000
rho <- 0.9
theta <- numeric(n_iter)
theta[1] <- 10
for (t in seq(2, n_iter)) {
  theta[t] <- rho * theta[t - 1] + stats::rnorm(1)
}
kept <- theta[-(1:1000)]
c(
  mean = mean(kept),
  variance = stats::var(kept),
  stationary_variance = 1 / (1 - rho^2)
) |>
  round(2)
```
:::
